description: Payment Village at DEF CON 33 explores payment system security, point-of-sale systems, ATM exploitation, contactless transaction protocols, and financial fraud. Talks cover carding market evolution, AI-driven fraud testing, pig butchering scam tracking, and ATM physical penetration.

talks.title: Carding is Dead, Long Live Carding
talks.teaser: Analyzes the rise of NFC relay Malware-as-a-Service platforms and Android banking trojans that bypass contactless payment security for large-scale card-present fraud.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Modern Carding Operations

Payment fraud has evolved beyond traditional card skimming into sophisticated Near Field Communication (NFC) relay attacks. Modern threat actors leverage mobile malware and coordinated physical relay networks to execute unauthorized contactless transactions in real time.

Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) Ecosystems

Turn-key NFC relay platforms, such as Supercard X, operate under a Malware-as-a-Service model. Developers distribute ready-to-use mobile payloads, management web panels, and proxy relays to global criminal affiliates, lowering technical barriers for illicit operations.

Technical Mechanics of NFC Relay Attacks

In an NFC relay attack, malware installed on a victim's smartphone intercepts NFC communication during legitimate tap operations or simulated terminal interactions. The intercepted cryptographic APDU commands are relayed via low-latency proxies to an accomplice's device positioned at a point-of-sale terminal, authorizing fraudulent charges.

Integration into Android Banking Trojans

Established Android banking trojan families are integrating NFC relay capabilities alongside overlay attacks and SMS interception. Countering this threat requires banks and payment processors to deploy behavioral anomaly detection and enforce strict transaction timing checks.

talks.title: Red Teaming Fraud Prevention Systems with GenAI
talks.teaser: Explores how generative AI and large language models can be leveraged to simulate sophisticated adversary techniques and test the resilience of fraud prevention systems.
talks.summary:
The Shifting Landscape of Financial Fraud

Financial fraudsters continually innovate to circumvent fraud detection rules, synthetic identity filters, and transaction monitoring algorithms. The emergence of generative AI and LLMs enables attackers to automate and scale deceptive workflows with unprecedented variation.

Simulating Adversarial Fraud with LLMs

Defenders and red teams can harness large language models to simulate realistic attacker personas, synthesize varied social engineering lures, and generate novel transactional fraud patterns. Automating these permutations allows organizations to proactively evaluate detection rules against emerging techniques.

Stress-Testing Detection Models and Behavioral Filters

Running automated red team simulations against production fraud engines exposes edge-case vulnerabilities, blind spots in identity verification pipelines, and latency in transaction risk scoring.

Building Resilient Adaptive Defenses

Strengthening fraud prevention requires incorporating multi-modal behavioral telemetry, dynamic risk scoring, and continuous model re-training to detect AI-generated fraud attempts before unauthorized transactions clear.

talks.title: Scamming Scammers: Weaponizing OSS Against Pig Butchering, Organized Crime
talks.teaser: Details the technical and operational mechanics behind global pig butchering scams and demonstrates how open-source intelligence tools are used to disrupt fraud rings.
talks.summary:
The Global Scope of Pig Butchering Scams

Pig butchering scams have caused tens of billions of dollars in losses worldwide, operated by transnational organized crime syndicates running industrial-scale scam compounds across Southeast Asia. These operations blend psychological manipulation with sophisticated cyber infrastructure.

Technical Infrastructure of Scam Compounds

Criminal syndicates manage elaborate networks of fake cryptocurrency trading platforms, malicious web applications, VoIP spoofing systems, and money laundering funnels. Forced labor and human trafficking victims are coerced into running multi-month social engineering campaigns targeting global marks.

Operation Shamrock and OSS Countermeasures

Law enforcement and open-source intelligence practitioners collaborate under initiatives like Operation Shamrock to track illicit crypto flows, identify fraudulent infrastructure, and seize stolen digital assets before liquidation.

Mobilizing Community and Technical Defense

Security researchers and investigators leverage open-source intelligence tools, blockchain analytics, and community reporting to map syndicate networks, alert potential victims, and assist law enforcement in disrupting criminal operations.

talks.title: How Extra Features in Contactless Payments Break Security, What We Can Do
talks.teaser: Examines how extra features and protocol extensions in contactless payment systems introduce security vulnerabilities, proposing fixes for payment terminals.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers how extra features in contactless payments break security, what we can do.

talks.title: Take All My Money: Penetrating ATMs
talks.teaser: Shares war stories, tooling, and operational hurdles from physical and logical penetration tests against automated teller machines (ATMs).
talks.summary:
ATM Penetration Testing Realities

Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) combine physical security safes, specialized embedded hardware, and standard desktop operating systems. Penetration testing these machines requires navigating both logical software defenses and heavy physical security barriers.

Hardware Interception and Dispenser Attacks

Logical attacks against ATMs frequently exploit vulnerabilities in the communication bus between the core PC and the cash dispenser unit. Attackers connect hardware implants directly to internal USB or serial buses to issue unauthorized dispense commands, known as black-box attacks.

Operating System and Application Weaknesses

Legacy ATM operating systems often run unhardened Windows environments with weak application whitelisting and insecure maintenance accounts. Misconfigured kiosk modes and diagnostic utilities allow testers to break out to administrative command prompts.

Defensive Mitigations for Financial Terminals

Securing ATM fleets requires implementing end-to-end cryptographic communication between dispenser controllers and core software, enforcing strict full-disk encryption, and supervising physical enclosure tamper sensors.
